other.about: The parts palette (compound ships, CM13): every part in the one part format (packages/ui-contract/src/parts.ts). Real stages, engines, power sources, arrays, dishes and a bay with the figures they flew with and the year they first flew; generic primitives with geometry only. Physics names only (ruling 14A.5). Built by scripts/build-base-parts.py; do not edit by hand.

mass_by_kind.why: a Dawn solar wing: almost 63 kg over 8.3 m by 2.3 m
an ISS heat rejection radiator: 1,122.64 kg over 23.3 m by 3.4 m deployed
the ISS Destiny laboratory: 14,515 kg in a can 8.5 m long and 4.3 m across, before racks
ISS Node 1: 11,895 kg in a can 5.5 m long and 4.3 m across
the Multi-Purpose Logistics Module: 4,082 kg empty in a can 6.6 m long and 4.57 m across

NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive and each craft's own source as the Sol today pack's craft.json names it (store-packs/sol-today/craft.json).

sources.nssdca: NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive and each craft's own source as the Sol today pack's craft.json names it (store-packs/sol-today/craft.json).
sources.idss: International Docking System Standard (IDSS) Interface Definition Document, revision E, 2016: an 800 mm passage. https://www.internationaldockingstandard.com/ (from memory, unverified).
sources.cbm: Common Berthing Mechanism on the International Space Station: a 50 inch (1.27 m) square passage (from memory, unverified).
sources.authored: authored for play and pictures; in the fudge register
sources.wiki-engines: Wikipedia, Comparison of orbital rocket engines, the Mass (kg) column, read 28 Nov 2026 (RS-25 3,526; F-1 8,391; J-2 1,438; Merlin 1D FT 470; AJ10-190 118). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comparison_of_orbital_rocket_engines (unverified: the page does not say dry or wet; liquid rows carry no 'with fuel' label).
sources.nasa-std-5001b: NASA-STD-5001B with Change 3 (2022), Structural design and test factors of safety for spaceflight hardware, section 4.2.1 Table 1: metallic structures, ultimate design factor 1.4, yield design factor 1.25 (protoflight). https://standards.nasa.gov/standard/nasa/nasa-std-5001 (unverified).
sources.nasa-tnd6876: Szabo, S. V. and Groesbeck, W. A. 1972, Centaur space vehicle pressurized propellant feed system tests, NASA TN D-6876, page 20: the flight-weight Centaur tank 'was structurally limited to maximum tank pressures of 19.6 N/cm2 (28.5 psia) in the hydrogen tank and 27.6 N/cm2 (40.0 psia) in the liquid oxygen tank'. https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/19720025206/downloads/19720025206.pdf (unverified).
sources.nss-iss-elements: International Space Station reference guide, Elements chapter (NASA; the copy at nss.org, an edition before Node 3 flew): Destiny length 8.5 m, diameter 4.3 m, mass 14,515 kg; Node 1 length 5.5 m, diameter 4.3 m, mass 11,895 kg. https://nss.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/ISS-International-Space-Station-03-Elements.pdf (unverified).
sources.nasa-iss-atcs: NASA, International Space Station active thermal control system overview: 'Each Radiator ORU measures 76.4 feet (23.3 meters) by 11.2 feet (3.4 meters) and weighs 2,475 pounds (1,122.64 kilograms)'. https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/473486main_iss_atcs_overview.pdf (unverified).
sources.jpl-dawn-launch: NASA/JPL 2007, Dawn launch press kit, Quick Facts: 'Two 8.3-meter-by-2.3-meter (27-foot-by-8-foot) solar panels ... Each wing weighs almost 63 kilograms (139 pounds).' https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/news/press_kits/dawn-launch.pdf (unverified).
sources.wiki-mplm: Wikipedia, Multi-Purpose Logistics Module, specifications: length 6.6 m, width 4.57 m, mass 4,082 kg empty, read 28 Nov 2026 (the body text says about 4,400 kg). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multi-Purpose_Logistics_Module (unverified).
sources.geometry: geometry: volume is length times radius squared (a lathe's frustums); outer area its side and ends
